competitive_position.claim: Xeris commercializes Recorlev, Gvoke, and Keveyis in the United States and is advancing XP-8121 using its proprietary XeriSol and XeriJect formulation platforms.
quotes: We have three commercially available products in the United States: Recorlev, a cortisol synthesis inhibitor for the treatment of endogenous hypercortisolemia in patients with Cushing's syndrome; Gvoke, a ready-to-use liquid glucagon for the treatment of severe hypoglycemia; and Keveyis, a therapy for primary periodic paralysis ("PPP").

We also have a pipeline of development programs led by XP-8121, a Phase 3-ready, once-weekly subcutaneous ("SC") levothyroxine injection for the treatment of hypothyroidism, as well as multiple early-stage programs that use our proprietary technology platforms, XeriSol and XeriJect, for ourselves and our partners.

competitive_position.claim: Recorlev holds U.S. orphan drug exclusivity through December 30, 2028 and patent protection through 2040, and is distributed via Xeris's CareConnection program and a single specialty pharmacy.
quotes: Recorlev has received orphan drug exclusivity status in the United States through December 30, 2028 and patent protection through 2040.

In addition, our efforts include the support of a single, highly experienced specialty pharmacy that provides logistical assistance in the securing of coverage from third-party payors and then subsequent distribution of Recorlev to patients.

The latter includes United States Patent Nos. 11,020,393, 11,278,547, 11,903,940, and 12,377,096, which were granted on June 1, 2021, March 22, 2022, February 20, 2024, and August 5, 2025, respectively, and which provide patent protection through 2040 for the use of Recorlev in the treatment of certain patients with persistent or recurrent Cushing's syndrome.

quotes: Net revenue increased by $75.0 million or 116.7% for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.
The increase was due to higher volume ($79.6 million or 123.9%), primarily driven by increased patient demand, offset by unfavorable net pricing ($4.6 million or 7.2%).

Net product revenue in the third quarter grew more than 43% year-over-year, led by Recorlev, where our expanded commercial team moved from build to yield and delivered record referrals and new patient starts.

competitive_position.claim: Recorlev faces direct competition in Cushing's syndrome from marketed therapies Korlym, Signifor LAR, and Isturisa, off-label generic ketoconazole, and Corcept's Phase 3 candidate relacorilant.
quotes: Recorlev competes primarily with other established medications and therapies, including older generic drugs that are used off-label for Recorlev's approved indication.

To our knowledge, the products used for the treatment of endogenous Cushing's syndrome patients who fail or are ineligible for surgery in the United States and Europe are: Korlym (mifepristone) marketed by Corcept Therapeutics in the United States; Signifor LAR (pasireotide) and Isturisa (osilodrostat), both marketed by Recordati in the United States and European Union ("EU"); and ketoconazole, metyrapone and mitotane marketed by HRA in the EU.
Corcept is developing relacorilant, a second-generation glucocorticoid receptor modulator; currently in Phase 3.

Regulatory approval of ketoconazole for the treatment of endogenous Cushing's syndrome in the United States, which is not currently being sought by any sponsor to our knowledge, could significantly increase competition for Recorlev due to the similar mechanisms of action between the drug products.

competitive_position.claim: Gvoke provides a ready-to-use, room-temperature stable liquid glucagon backed by XeriSol composition-of-matter patents expiring in 2036, addressing more than 14 million U.S. diabetes patients at risk of severe hypoglycemia.
quotes: Gvoke is available in three presentation types: Gvoke HypoPen (auto-injector), Gvoke PFS (pre-filled syringe), and Gvoke Kit (pre-filled vial and administration syringe).
As of October 30, 2026, we owned 197 patents issued globally, including composition of matter patents covering our ready-to-use glucagon formulation that expire in 2036.

We estimate that more than 14 million people in the United States are at heightened risk of severe hypoglycemia and, per guidelines issued by the American Diabetes Association and others, should have a ready-to-use glucagon product like the Gvoke HypoPen with them at all times.

competitive_position.claim: Xeris's XeriSol and XeriJect non-aqueous formulation platforms are supported by 70 granted patents globally and active collaborations with several major pharmaceutical companies.
quotes: Our proprietary non-aqueous XeriSol and XeriJect technologies offer the opportunity to eliminate the need for reconstitution and refrigeration, enable long-term stability, significantly reduce injection volume, and allow for a more convenient SC or IM administration as opposed to IV infusion and other routes of administration.

Included in the total patents, we have 70 granted patents globally related to our platform technologies and nine patents granted in the United States and listed in the FDA Orange Book covering proprietary formulations of levoketoconazole (the active pharmaceutical ingredient in Recorlev) and the uses of such formulations in treating certain endocrine-related diseases and syndromes.
We are currently collaborating with several major pharmaceutical companies on the development of formulations of their proprietary therapeutics.

competitive_position.claim: Pipeline candidate XP-8121 targets over 20 million U.S. hypothyroidism patients with a once-weekly subcutaneous injection protected by U.S. Patent No. 12,751,937 expiring October 19, 2043, addressing absorption and adherence limits of daily oral levothyroxine.
quotes: Hypothyroidism affects over 20 million people in the United States.

XP-8121 is designed to be a once-weekly, small-volume, subcutaneous injection that, given its route of administration, bypasses the gastrointestinal tract and could avoid many of the therapeutic complications associated with the use of oral forms of levothyroxine.

On October 6, 2026, the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) granted Xeris U.S. Patent No. 12,751,937, entitled “Stable Levothyroxine Compositions In Aprotic Polar Solvents,” which is expected to expire on October 19, 2043.
